units.source_text: 他在身心俱疲的时候，偶然读到拉迪格临终遗言，他感觉到自己再次听见了众神的笑声。

en.t: When he was exhausted in body and mind, he happened to read Radiguet's dying words, and felt as though he had once again heard the laughter of the gods.

units.source_text: 就是那句话：“神兵来捉我。”

en.t: It was that sentence: "The divine soldiers are coming to seize me."

units.source_text: 他想和他的迷信和感伤主义战斗。

en.t: He wanted to fight against his own superstition and sentimentalism.

units.source_text: 可是从肉体上来说，他已经无能为力了。

en.t: But physically speaking, he was already powerless.

units.source_text: 毫无疑问，“世纪末的恶魔”正在摧残折磨他。

en.t: Without a doubt, the "demon of the fin de siecle" was ravaging and tormenting him.

units.source_text: 他羡慕那些虔信神的中世纪的人们。

en.t: He envied those people of the Middle Ages who devoutly believed in God.

units.source_text: 但是他最终也不可能信神——信仰神的爱。

en.t: But in the end, he too could not believe in God, could not believe in God's love.

units.source_text: 可是就连柯克托都是相信神的啊！

en.t: And yet even Cocteau believed in God!
